title: Admon ben Gadai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: At [the beginning of Mishnah Ketubot, chapter 13](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Ketubot.13.1), the two judges of penalties in Jerusalem are Admon and Chanan ben Avishalom. The Gemara, [Ketubot 105a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.105a.2), gives Admon ben Gadai. Seven rulings of his remain in the Mishnah; Rabban Gamliel endorses three with “Admon’s words seem right to me.” One is familiar to everyone: “[Have I lost out because I am male?](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Ketubot.13.3)”

notes.text: The linked Mishnah names two judges of decrees; the Bavli’s baraita names three judges of robbery cases, with Admon identified as ben Gadai. Rabban Gamliel supports Admon in the linked inheritance case, in [the case about jars of oil](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Ketubot.13.4), and in [the case about a promised dowry](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Ketubot.13.5). [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=250&lang=en) cites the chapter and its other parallels.
